hints: Focus on what hot aluminium oxide does to an alcohol, think elimination of water to form a C=C double bond.
Dehydration of propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, removes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to give propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$.
Remember how an alkene reacts with $\text{Br}_2$, both Br atoms add across the double bond to neighbouring carbons.
walkthrough:
**Dehydrate the alcohol to find the hydrocarbon**

Dehydration is an elimination reaction. Hot $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ removes water from the alcohol to form an alkene.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So the hydrocarbon is propene.

**Add bromine to the alkene**

Alkenes undergo electrophilic addition with bromine. The $\text{C=C}$ pi bond breaks and one Br adds to each of the two double-bonded carbons.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$$
This is a dibromoalkane with Br on carbon 1 and carbon 2.

**Match to the displayed structure**

The product must have 3 carbons, 6 hydrogens and 2 bromines, with the two Br atoms on adjacent carbons. That is 1,2-dibromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{-CHBr-CH}_2\text{Br}$.

options.A: This is 1-bromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. It has only one Br, so it cannot come from addition of $\text{Br}_2$ to an alkene. Students may pick this by confusing bromine addition with substitution or with addition of HBr.
options.B: This is 2-bromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3$. Again it has only one Br. This is the Markovnikov product of propene with HBr, not with $\text{Br}_2$, so it is a classic HBr versus Br2 trap.
options.C: This is 1,1-dibromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBr}_2$, with both Br atoms on the same end carbon. Addition to a C=C must place the Br atoms on neighbouring carbons, not both on carbon 1.
options.D: This is 1,2-dibromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$. The middle carbon has one Br and the right-hand carbon has one Br, exactly what you expect when $\text{Br}_2$ adds across $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$. Well done, this is the correct addition product.
